title: What is @Conditional and its variants? What is the difference between @SpringBootApplication and @EnableAutoConfiguration? What are the differences between Spring Boot, Spring Framework, and Spring MVC?
keyPoints: @Conditional registers a bean only when a runtime condition is met
@ConditionalOnClass activates auto-configuration when a library is on the classpath
@ConditionalOnMissingBean backs off so your custom bean always wins over auto-config
@ConditionalOnProperty enables feature flags without changing code
Spring Framework is the core IoC and DI container, Spring MVC is the web layer on the Servlet API, and Spring Boot adds opinionated auto-configuration with an embedded server

s1_definition.oneliner: @Conditional registers beans only when a runtime condition is met, and @SpringBootApplication combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan into a single annotation.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **@Conditional** – registers a bean only when a specific condition evaluates to true at startup.
- **@ConditionalOnClass** – activates a configuration when a given class exists on the classpath, which is how starter dependencies trigger auto-configuration.
- **@ConditionalOnMissingBean** – backs off when the developer has already defined a bean of that type, so custom configuration always wins.
- **@ConditionalOnProperty** – creates a bean only when a specific property is set to a specific value, enabling feature flags.
- **@SpringBootApplication** – a convenience annotation that combines `@Configuration` (marks the class as a bean source), `@EnableAutoConfiguration` (triggers classpath-based auto-configuration), and `@ComponentScan` (discovers annotated components in the package and its sub-packages).
s1_definition.analogy: Think of a bank branch opening for the day. The branch manager checks conditions before assigning roles: hire a vault guard only if the branch has a vault (@ConditionalOnClass), use the default cash counter only if no one has already set up a custom one (@ConditionalOnMissingBean), and enable the foreign exchange desk only if the regional memo says forex is enabled (@ConditionalOnProperty). @SpringBootApplication is the grand opening checklist that registers the branch, auto-sets up equipment, and recruits staff in one step.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The @Conditional annotation is the foundation of Spring Boot's auto-configuration. When Spring Boot starts, it reads auto-configuration classes from the classpath and evaluates their conditions. @ConditionalOnClass checks whether a library is available, which is how adding a starter dependency automatically triggers the matching configuration. @ConditionalOnMissingBean checks whether you have already defined a bean of the same type, and backs off if you have, so your custom configuration always wins. @ConditionalOnProperty checks a configuration value, enabling feature flags that control which beans are created without any if-else logic in code.

@SpringBootApplication is the single annotation that every Spring Boot main class carries. It combines @Configuration to mark the class as a bean source, @EnableAutoConfiguration to trigger classpath-based auto-configuration, and @ComponentScan to discover all annotated components in the package tree. Pankaj places the main class in the root package so every sub-package is scanned automatically.

Spring Framework provides the core IoC container with dependency injection and AOP. Spring MVC adds the web layer with DispatcherServlet and controllers on top of the Servlet API. Spring Boot adds opinionated auto-configuration, an embedded server, starter dependencies, and production-ready features like Actuator. In the National Bank of India's microservices, each service uses Spring Boot with conditional annotations to get sensible defaults from shared starters while retaining the ability to override any bean with a custom implementation.

Remember one sentence: @Conditional makes Spring Boot smart enough to configure itself based on what is on the classpath, what you have already defined, and what your properties say.
